answer: One defence is a sequential puzzle ladder. Each epoch the network hands every agent a seed, and the agent must solve twelve hash puzzles in order, each seeded by the last solution, so no shortcut runs them in parallel; solutions are signed and pinned publicly, and an out-of-order chain or copied solution freezes the identity and burns its $40 bond. Forging 10,000 fakes costs $400,000 in bonds plus 20,000 GPU-hours at $1.20 an hour, about $424,000 and 83 days of work. It is the old fable of the lotus opening one petal at a time: rush it and the ember of proof goes out, leaving only ash.
